item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find a Tinubu-authored 2024 source that directly and specifically addresses nuclear risk reduction. The strongest nuclear evidence was Nigeria’s defense ministry UN disarmament statement, which is official but indirect. The record is mixed but weakly positive: administration-level support for nuclear disarmament, counterterrorism cooperation, and regional de-escalation was counterbalanced by coercive, military-forward domestic-security rhetoric.","evidence":[{"title":"Honourable Minister of Defence of Nigeria Addresses the United Nations on Nuclear Disarmament","publisher":"Ministry of Defence, Nigeria","date":"September 28, 2024","url":"https://defence.gov.ng/2024/09/28/honourable-minister-of-defence-of-nigeria-addresses-the-united-nations-on-nuclear-disarmament/","summary":"Nigeria publicly reaffirmed commitment to nuclear disarmament and non-proliferation, urged NPT compliance, endorsed the TPNW, and said it supported peaceful nuclear energy under IAEA monitoring. This is the clearest direct evidence in the 2024 record for lowering nuclear risk, though it is ministerial rather than a Tinubu-authored statement.","question_ids":["1B.1"]},{"title":"President Tinubu Calls for Suspension of Sanctions on Guinea, Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso","publisher":"State House, Nigeria","date":"February 24, 2024","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-calls-for-suspension-of-sanctions-on-guinea-mali-niger-burkina-faso/","summary":"Tinubu argued that sanctions had become ineffective and should be abandoned in favor of a “better path” through negotiation and improved governance. This is relevant as de-escalatory regional diplomacy, even though it is not nuclear-specific.","question_ids":["1B.1"]},{"title":"President Tinubu Meets FBI Director, Calls for Stronger Collaboration to Fight Cybercrime and Terrorism","publisher":"State House, Nigeria","date":"June 14, 2024","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-meets-fbi-director-calls-for-stronger-collaboration-to-fight-cybercrime-and-terrorism/","summary":"Tinubu called for closer cooperation to fight terrorism and cybercrime and said his administration was working to eliminate those threats. This supports a reading of risk reduction, especially against non-state violence and transnational crime.","question_ids":["1B.1"]},{"title":"President Tinubu’s Broadcast on the Nationwide Protest","publisher":"State House, Nigeria","date":"August 4, 2024","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-broadcast-on-the-nationwide-protest/","summary":"Tinubu acknowledged deaths, destruction, and unrest during nationwide protests tied to economic hardship and bad governance. This is relevant context for 2024 risk conditions, but it does not itself show nuclear-risk reduction.","question_ids":["1B.1"]},{"title":"President Tinubu’s Statement on the Killings of Soldiers in Aba","publisher":"State House, Nigeria","date":"June 2, 2024","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-statement-on-the-killings-of-soldiers-in-aba/","summary":"Tinubu used forceful language, saying the government would “come down heavily” on attackers and had the capacity to crush violent non-state actors. This cuts the other way on the lens: it reflects coercive escalation in internal security, even if framed as restoring order.","question_ids":["1B.1"]},{"title":"President Tinubu: I’ll Do All Within My Powers To Equip, Arm The Military","publisher":"State House, Nigeria","date":"August 23, 2024","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-ill-do-all-within-my-powers-to-equip-arm-the-military/","summary":"Tinubu vowed to continue equipping and arming the military and emphasized security assets and military readiness. This is not nuclear escalation, but it is evidence of a militarized response style rather than a narrowly humanitarian or risk-minimizing posture.","question_ids":["1B.1"]}]}
